title: Responses event-model translation and fidelity runbook
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Background: As part of the OpenAI Responses compatibility effort, we need a deterministic translation layer between our native streaming/event model and the OpenAI Responses event envelope. Previous audits surfaced intermittent fidelity gaps for tool/function-call events, chunked structured outputs, and user/system role metadata. Goals: 1) Define a canonical translation contract for every surfaced event type (message, delta, function_call, tool_invocation, structured schema validation events, end-of-stream). 2) Create a runbook and reference impl for translating inbound Responses streams into Redwood's internal events with lossless semantics wherever possible. 3) Define explicit, observable fallback semantics when exact parity is impossible (e.g., partial tool call payloads or mixed text+tool-deltas). Scope: - Map and test streaming deltas, chunked JSON outputs, and tool/function call start/complete events. - Provide example mappings for function/tool arguments, error propagation, and structured-output schema enforcement. - Implement translation helpers in the runtime shim and a test harness for fuzzing edge cases. Non-goals: - Replacing the canonical API surface (we are building a compatibility layer, not modifying customer-facing SDKs). - Full backward compatibility for deprecated OpenAI behaviors outside streaming/function-call domain.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A published 'canonical translation contract' doc (Confluence) covering all event types and their Redwood equivalents.
2) Reference implementation checkin: runtime shim + unit tests that convert a curated Responses stream corpus into internal events with >=99% fidelity for key fields (message content, role, function_call name/args, structured JSON atoms).
3) End-to-end integration test demonstrating tool invocation from Responses client -> Redwood shim -> backend tool executor -> function return is surfaced back to Responses-compatible stream.
4) Metrics and alerts added to Console: translation errors, dropped-delta counts, and schema-validation failures.
5) Rollout playbook that includes canary traffic routing and an automatic rollback trigger on translation error rate > 0.1% over 5m.
design_notes:
Key design decisions and trade-offs:
- Canonical envelope: introduce a minimal 'redwood_event' envelope with fields: event_type, seq, origin_span, canonical_payload. This allows us to preserve sequence IDs and attribute provenance without mutating original Responses payloads.
- Fidelity-first mapping: where possible preserve raw delta fragments and rehydrate into internal tokens; but for large chunked JSON we will store a compressed 'raw_chunk' blob plus a validated JSON "decoded" field for downstream routing.
- Tool/function calls: map 'tool_call.start' and 'tool_call.complete' to separate events and attach correlated call_id. If Responses supplies partial args across deltas, we will buffer until `call_complete` or until size/timeout. Timeout policy default: 3s additional buffering before emitting "incomplete_tool_call" event with descriptive metadata.
- Structured outputs: implement an opt-in strict-schema validation mode that rejects streams failing schema validation; default runtime behavior is 'best-effort' with a validation failure event emitted so engineers can create regression alerts.
- Backwards-compatibility trade-off: we will not attempt to emulate deprecated noise behaviors; instead we document differences in the contract and provide a migration guide.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 - Spec and examples (3 days): create canonical mapping doc, example streams, and a corpus of problematic cases harvested from previous support tickets and logs.
Phase 2 - Reference shim and tests (7 days): implement translation utilities in runtime-compat module, add unit tests for mapping rules, create simulated Responses stream generator.
Phase 3 - Integration harness + CI (5 days): wire shim into staging runtime, run E2E tests calling a mock tool execution service, measure fidelity metrics.
Phase 4 - Canary rollout + observability (2 days): deploy to 5% of traffic behind canary routing, add dashboards and alerts.
Phase 5 - Full rollout + docs (2 days): expand to 100% traffic and publish migration guide + runbook.
Implementation subtasks (each created as sub-issues):
- ENG-37522: spec doc + corpus
- ENG-37523: runtime-compat translation library
- ENG-37524: fuzz/integration harness
- ENG-37525: monitoring & alerts
- ENG-37526: docs and runbook
qa_plan: Unit tests for every mapping rule with both happy-path and malformed fragments. Property-based fuzzing that injects delta reordering, truncated JSON chunks, and mixed tool/text deltas. Integration tests: mock Responses client -> shim -> mock tool executor -> Responses-compatible response. Test acceptance threshold: translation error rate < 0.1% on curated corpus; schema validation alerts generated and surfaced in test dashboard.
rollout: Canary at 5% for 24h, monitor translation_error_rate, dropped_delta_ratio, end_to_end_latency. Automatic rollback if translation_error_rate > 0.1% sustained for 5 minutes or if customer-facing errors spike. Post-rollout: 72h monitoring window and one-week retrospective to capture unseen edge cases.
